notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 6th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 39%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Artemi Panarin has not dressed for the last 4 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Alex Turcotte has taken his spot beside Adrian Kempe and Alex Laferriere.
Trevor Moore is day to day and has missed the last 2 games.
Erik Gustafsson is day to day (upper-body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-pair defenseman.

Artemi Panarin is expected back after missing 4 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.

Mike Matheson is out about 3-4 weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Noah Dobson has taken his spot beside Kaiden Guhle. That pair has had 28% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 37:03 together, down from 54% with Matheson.

Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 29% of the team’s shorthanded time in 23 games, up from 6% last season.

MTL.head: A slightly uphill night for the Canadiens
MTL.body: Even though Montréal has home-ice advantage, Los Angeles has been out-chancing opponents lately and gets Panarin back. The Canadiens can tip it if they keep the shots coming.

LAK.head: The Kings have a slight edge
LAK.body: Even though Montréal has home-ice advantage, Los Angeles has been out-chancing opponents lately and gets Panarin back. The Canadiens can still swing it if they keep the shots coming.

story.head: Panarin’s favorite opponent
paras: The Kings (7-12-2) lost 4-2 to Ottawa on Saturday, and the Canadiens (14-6-4) lost 4-3 to Philadelphia the same night. Going in, the Kings are seventh in the Pacific (tied for 30th in the NHL) and the Canadiens third in the Atlantic (tied for sixth).

The Kings have played better than their record (.381) says: their chances are worth about .603, and their finishing has held them back. The Canadiens’ record (.667) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.548), largely because they’re 9-6 in one-goal games.

The Kings leave the shooting to their forwards (2nd lowest) and forecheck as hard as almost anyone (3rd). They also keep dangerous shots away better than almost anyone (2nd), so the Kings keep dangerous shots away, but the Canadiens give up a lot of them. The Habs get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (4th), but take more penalties than they draw (31st). The Canadiens’ struggling power play gets a tough test from the Kings’ penalty killers.

Artemi Panarin (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 17 GP) leads the Kings in scoring, with a point in nine straight games against Montréal. Adrian Kempe (6 G / 8 A / 14 P in 20 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Canadiens, Lane Hutson (5 G / 19 A / 24 P in 24 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Cole Caufield (12 G / 8 A / 20 P in 24 GP) has a team-high twelve goals.
Darcy Kuemper (7-5-1 / .885 SV% in 13 GS) is expected to go for Los Angeles. Jakub Dobeš (4-3-2 / .864 SV% in 9 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Montréal, but is expected to start.
